info.title: Cisco Enterprise Networking App for Splunk

release.notes:
Changes since v4.0.0. The App and TA release independently: App v4.0.20 requires TA v4.0.50 or later. This entry describes source changes, not publication or production qualification.

##### Dashboards and usability

* **Search correctness:** Corrected logical operators in Overview client-health and Security Insights firewall searches. Removed the Performance dashboard dependency on an unavailable ThousandEyes account-group lookup; groups display their IDs.
* **Multi-Manager Change Audit:** Added friendly Manager/input labels and exact source isolation across all searches, event details and configuration comparisons. Submitted and deep-linked filters remain authoritative; All Time trends use adaptive buckets.
* **Readiness diagnostics:** Added a direct link to the strict-versus-retained diagnostic search. Extra retained summaries appear as collapsed informational compatibility details instead of a not-ready warning.
* **Talker and sensor analysis:** Restored Top 10 Talkers drilldowns and added a keyboard-operable Talker details selector. Temperature and humidity charts rank at most ten sensors by peak absolute deviation from each sensor's selected-window average.
* **Charts:** All line charts connect across missing values. Optical power and temperature charts are full-width, offer interface and Rx/Tx filters, and plot at most ten series while retaining matching power violations in a summary table. Hidden host filters initialize correctly, and click-time helper fields no longer appear as series.
* **Tables and actions:** Master Endpoint Record displays up to 1,000 rows per page with scrolling. Studio tables have more canvas space and readable column widths; Open in Search and visualization actions remain available.
* **Status colors:** Restored door-status and Meraki Policy Sync series colors, URL reputation and endpoint completeness table colors, and compliance-card/table colors. Zero failures are green, positive failures are red, and skipped, unavailable or unrecognized requirement states are amber. Severity cards use colored values on white backgrounds.
* **Maps and navigation:** Corrected Overview coordinate bindings and added public-IP geolocation fallback. Private addresses require configured ISE location coordinates. Renamed the experimental home dashboard to Overview Beta, distinguished Performance Insights from Cisco IOS Performance, and standardized Implementation Metrics labels.
* **Lookup maintenance:** The asset reaper keeps endpoints with valid, non-expired ISE last-seen timestamps and rewrites the KV lookup to remove expired records. Scheduled lookup jobs retain a single `rows_written` summary after writing, while the reaper retains its purge metric. The summary counts submitted rows; it does not independently verify write success or final lookup size.

##### Compatibility, security and packaging

* **TA requirement:** Package dependencies and Overview readiness require Cisco Enterprise Networking Add-on v4.0.50 or later. Older, missing or malformed TA versions fail readiness.
* **Retained-data compatibility:** Catalyst Center client health, compliance, Device Health, Issue, network health, Security Advisory and Client datasets use TA-owned transition eventtypes. ISE FullReport, Hardware and Registry datasets and asset builders also cover both current and historical report sourcetypes. The App does not duplicate the TA eventtype definitions.
* **Dataset constraints:** Added validated constraints for ISE System Health, Syslog Analytics Reports and Application Access, and Cyber Vision Device Vulnerability Events. These retain supported analytics and nested vulnerability records.
* **Dependency updates:** Updated brace-expansion, fast-uri, js-yaml, Moment, colord and qs for reported advisories. Current advisory and release qualification checks remain separate.
* **Package cleanup:** Excluded 16 replaced Simple XML dashboards while retaining their Studio replacements and repository reference originals. Archives include version and build in `cisco-catalyst-app-<version>-<build>.tgz`, with validation against packaged metadata.

##### Upgrade actions

1. Install TA v4.0.50 or later on the collecting tier and search head, then upgrade the App to v4.0.20. Review customer local eventtype overrides if readiness reports an unavailable definition.
2. Hard-refresh open dashboard and editor tabs after upgrading.
3. Retained acceleration summaries remain usable with `allow_old_summaries=true`. Use a controlled rebuild only when transition-eventtype or specialized-dataset constraints must apply retroactively to retained historical buckets.
4. Validate the longest required time range, selected Manager isolation, table pagination, lookup inventory and scheduled jobs in a representative deployment before publication. Bounded plots and submitted-row counts do not establish fleet capacity or lookup completeness.

info.title: Cisco Enterprise Networking App for Splunk

releases.notes:
##### Compatibility and dashboards

* **TA compatibility preflight:** Overview now confirms that Cisco Enterprise Networking Add-on for Splunk 4.0.0 or later is installed and that the complete transition-eventtype contract is available. Missing, older, or incomplete TA deployments receive a persistent warning.
* **NetFlow search compatibility:** NetFlow searches, drilldowns, React search links, and data-model constraints use `eventtype=cisco_netflow`, covering production `stream:netflow` while excluding options metadata from Network Traffic scope.
* **SD-WAN access migration compatibility:** ACL and SGACL searches and data-model constraints use `cisco_sdwan_acl_logs` and `cisco_sdwan_sgacl_logs`, preserving current and retained sourcetype history without broadening unrelated data-model children.
* **Catalyst Center report migration compatibility:** Scheduled-report datasets use `cisco_dnac_inventory_report`, `cisco_dnac_compliance_report`, and `cisco_dnac_report` while retaining the existing dataset and field names.
* **Dashboard correctness:** Invalid data-model fields, an undeclared Cyber Vision host token, empty drilldown conditions, incorrect Security Insights filters, and SD-WAN/Meraki Security Events time-series selectors were corrected.
* **Bounded dashboard work:** The Security Events timeline now uses two data-model scans instead of three, top-N panels use bounded sorts, and discarded sort or aggregation stages were removed from trend searches.
* **Navigation and branding:** Supported Splunk 10.4 navigation icons replace collapsed-menu letter monograms, and the packaged app icon and logo set align with the Cisco Enterprise Networking Add-on.
* **Search contract audit:** Automated coverage now checks classic dashboards, Dashboard Studio definitions, and scheduled searches for macro, token, data-model field, index, acceleration, and bounded-search contracts.

##### Security and build tooling

* **Patched dependency graph:** The Yarn dependency graph resolves the repository's current security advisories, removes the unused Lerna/Nx/npm publication subtree, and upgrades the packaging toolchain without adding `node_modules` to the installable Splunk app.
* **Smaller build surface:** The lockfile was reduced from 1,296 to 849 package resolutions while retaining the TypeScript, Tailwind, React, and Splunk packaging workflow. Node.js 20.9 or later is required only for building the app, not for running the packaged Splunk app.

##### Upgrade notes

* Install Cisco Enterprise Networking Add-on for Splunk **4.0.0** before App 4.0.0. The coordinated app depends on TA-owned transition eventtypes and does not bundle or redefine them.
* Rebuild existing `Cisco_Catalyst_App` data-model acceleration summaries after upgrading both packages because the NetFlow, SD-WAN access, and Catalyst Center report constraints changed.
* Keep `stream:netflow` in the app discovery macro and use `eventtype=cisco_netflow` in searches.
* Generic Custom API data remains outside broad CIM children; select it by its stable product sourcetype plus `endpoint_name` or `endpoint_path`.

info.title: Cisco Enterprise Networking App for Splunk

releases.notes:
#### Highlights

* **Product family alignment:** Standardized the product name as **Cisco Enterprise Networking App for Splunk**. The existing `cisco-catalyst-app` application ID and compatibility identifiers remain unchanged.
* **Dashboard modernization:** Migrated Cisco network-data dashboards to Dashboard Studio, added six operational intelligence dashboards, improved drilldowns and filter behavior, and retained classic dashboards under **All Legacy Dashboards**.
* **Consistent visual experience:** Applied an accessible Cisco C3 color system across Dashboard Studio, Simple XML, and the React landing page.
* **Expanded data model:** Added twelve source-specific datasets for Cisco Catalyst Center, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, Cisco Identity Services Engine, Cisco Meraki, and related operational data. The internal `Cisco_Catalyst_App` data-model identifier remains unchanged.
* **Improved search reliability:** Corrected invalid fields, unresolved tokens, ineffective drilldowns, wildcard handling, and dashboard searches that did not dispatch reliably.
* **Data-model acceleration visibility:** Added live acceleration status, stale-summary detection, controlled retained-summary support, and guidance for rebuilding summaries after an upgrade.
* **Reduced acceleration workload:** Changed summary maintenance from every 5 minutes to every 15 minutes, limited concurrent summarization, and retained the 7-day summary range.
* **Coordinated add-on compatibility:** The app now requires **Cisco Enterprise Networking Add-on for Splunk 4.0.0** or later. Cisco IOS enrichment is owned by the add-on rather than duplicated in the app.

#### Upgrade notes

* Install **Cisco Enterprise Networking Add-on for Splunk 4.0.0** before upgrading the app.
* Rebuild the `Cisco_Catalyst_App` acceleration summaries because the packaged data-model definition changed.
* Preserve any deployment-specific `cisco_catalyst_app_index` macro override. Include the ThousandEyes metric index when ThousandEyes data is collected.
* Use the Overview readiness checks to verify add-on compatibility and acceleration health after the upgrade.

info.title: Cisco Enterprise Networking for Splunk Platform

releases.notes:
Dashboards & Usability

  • SD-WAN Change Audit dashboard refreshed: Added clearer setup guidance, collapsible prerequisites, better panel descriptions, summary metrics, and a focused change explorer for reviewing vManage administrative changes from `cisco:sdwan:audit:logs`.
  • SD-WAN before/after configuration review improved: The dashboard now uses the collector-provided `audit_config_before` and `audit_config_after` fields directly, so config comparison panels no longer rely on fragile position-based audit detail reconstruction.
  • SD-WAN audit setup guidance added: The dashboard now explains that customers need Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk version 3.2.38 or later, an SD-WAN Audit Logs input, and both Audit Log Details and Config Difference enabled to populate the detail and config-diff views.
  • Overview setup guidance added: The Overview dashboard now links to the required Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk and provides a concise setup checklist for production deployments: scope index macros first, enable data model acceleration second, then set `summariesonly` to `true` after acceleration reaches 100.00% Completed.
  • Index macro setup improved: `cisco_catalyst_app_index` and `cisco_catalyst_sdwan_index` now default to all indexes so first-run dashboards can find data before local macro configuration. The Overview dashboard includes helper searches that return paste-ready macro values for production scoping.
  • Step Reports access cleanup: Removed stale metadata that referenced an undefined `cisco_catalyst_step_reports` role, so Step Reports inherit the normal app view permissions.
  • App metadata cleanup: Declared light and dark theme support and removed stale install/runtime metadata from the packaged app configuration.
  • Cyber Vision vulnerability overview corrected: Updated the vulnerability dashboard so it uses the correct app index macro and aligns with the dedicated `cisco:cybervision:vulnerabilities` sourcetype.

Data Models & Fields

  • Expanded Cisco Catalyst data model coverage: Added child datasets for Catalyst Center interface health (`cisco:dnac:devicehealth:interface`), Cyber Vision vulnerabilities (`cisco:cybervision:vulnerabilities`), Cyber Vision components (`cisco:cybervision:components`), Cyber Vision flows (`cisco:cybervision:flows`), and SD-WAN SSE tunnel health (`cisco:sdwan:ssetunnelhealth`).
  • Data model acceleration defaults clarified: The packaged Cisco Catalyst data model now defines a 7-day acceleration summary range and staggered 5-minute schedule for admins who enable acceleration. The Hunk-only DFS block-size setting was removed.
  • SD-WAN audit data model fields added: Added the new SD-WAN audit detail and before/after config fields produced by Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk 3.2.38 to the SD-WAN audit child dataset, including `audit_log_details`, `audit_config_before`, `audit_config_after`, and related summary fields.
  • SD-WAN audit user field corrected: Added the correctly spelled `audit_log_user` field and updated app content to use it while preserving the previous `audti_log_user` field for backward compatibility.
  • Cross-app data model searches fixed: Exported the Cisco Catalyst data model together with its required base-search macros, `cisco_catalyst_app_index` and `cisco_catalyst_app_sourcetypes`, so external apps can run `tstats` searches against `Cisco_Catalyst_App` without data model root-object cache errors.
  • Packaged metadata export handling fixed: Updated the packaging scrub step to keep app-wide metadata private while preserving explicit per-object exports required by shared knowledge objects.

Upgrade notes

  • Upgrade the Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk from Splunkbase to version 3.2.38 or later to populate the newest sourcetypes and SD-WAN audit config-diff fields used by this app.
  • For the SD-WAN Change Audit dashboard, create an Audit Logs input in the Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk and enable both Audit Log Details and Config Difference. Without that input, no `cisco:sdwan:audit:logs` data is collected; without those checkboxes, the detail and before/after config panels remain empty.
  • Before enabling data model acceleration, use the Overview dashboard helper searches to populate `cisco_catalyst_app_index` and `cisco_catalyst_sdwan_index`. The defaults search all indexes to avoid empty first-run dashboards, but scoped macros are strongly recommended for production performance and data boundaries.
  • If data model acceleration is enabled, use at least a 7-day summary range, or increase to 30 days or more if users search longer windows and the environment can support it. When acceleration status reaches 100.00% Completed, set the `summariesonly` macro to `summariesonly=true` for best dashboard performance.

info.title: Cisco Enterprise Networking for Splunk Platform

releases.notes:
Overview

Fixed

ISE Syslog System Health datamodel (Cisco\_Catalyst\_App)

Version 3.1.0 shipped a corrupted datamodel: the `ISE_Syslog_System_Health` child object was missing from the model while still referenced in metadata, and the parent `Cisco_Catalyst_ISE_Syslog_Events` constraints were overwritten. Panels depending on ISE syslog system-health data (CPU, memory, disk, RADIUS/TACACS latency) could return empty results.

Version 3.2.0 restores `ISE_Syslog_System_Health` and its seven calculated fields from the last known-good structure.

Changed

C2C / CYBERCOM compliance reporting pipeline

Compliance and Master Endpoint Record data is now materialized through a KV Store pipeline instead of running large inline searches at dashboard time.

  • New KV collection `cisco_catalyst_assets` (\~80 fields per endpoint)
  • Scheduled stage searches populate intermediate lookups; `cisco_catalyst_kv_update` merges them into `cisco_catalyst_assets_lookup` approximately every 10 minutes
  • `cisco_catalyst_assets_reaper` removes stale records (7-day retention)
  • Expanded posture rule-result macros for ICAM/C2C policy evaluation
  • Updated CYBERCOM device-category and access-level macros
  • Additional datamodel fields on ISE Full Reports and ISE Syslog Analytics

The following dashboards now read from the centralized asset lookup:

  • Overview Analytics Reports
  • Endpoint Compliance Analytics Reports
  • Master Endpoint Record Analytics Reports
  • Implementation Metrics
  • Step 1 Report (Device Classification)
  • Step 2 Report (Manageability and Compliance)
  • Step 3 Report (Compliance Remediation)
  • Step 4 Report (ICAM Summary)

Added

ISE endpoint manageability classification

  • Endpoints are classified as Managed, Manageable, or Unmanageable based on authentication, posture status, and CYBERCOM category
  • New `managed` field on the master asset record, used in Step 2 and Implementation Metrics
  • Endpoint Compliance dashboard: endpoints with populated rule-result fields are sorted ahead of rows with no rule results within each posture group
